page.layout: One page of text in a single column. Running head at the top, centred, with the page number at the top right. Catchword at the lower right and gathering signature at the lower left, below the last line.

main_text.p: perest remedium. Debeo etiam hostes & gentem inuisam adhibere, ut consolationem accipiam, atque uin-dictam summam de peccatis. Pulchrè exprimit adfectus patris dolentis, se talibus uti debere remediis, nempe crudelitate impiorum, et gentilium, ad puniendum suum populum.

Et repurgabo.) Effectus ultionis Divinæ, quem ad consolationem bonorum apparet esse subiectum. Bo-na enim necessariò sequuntur ex aduersis, quæ Dominus immittit: & percutit Dominus, ut sanet. Videtur subesse σαγηναγωγός[?].

Ciuitas est iusticiæ.) Sermocinatio. Fingit enim hæc verba ab aliis post plagas & emendationem ad laudem Reipub.melius constitutæ usurpanda. Familiare autem est propheticis hoc pacto, primò demonstra-re & arguere peccata: secundò, comminari & prædicere pœnas:tertiò, promittere vel ostendere bona ali-qua secutura. Id quod ad bonorum & resipiscentium consolationem proculdubio faciunt. Crebra habituri sumus huius consuetudinis exempla.
Contritio autem iniquorum.) Repetitio vindictæ ad fortius commouendum adfectus. Prius enim quàm restituatur Respubl. in melius, oportet om-nes iniustè agentes consumi.
QUONIAM confundentur.) Secundus locus, in quo concionatur contra idololatricos cultus. Mutatio personæ, ut hic, ubi prius in tertia persona ser

page.notes: Greek word after "subesse" (marked here as σαγηναγωγός[?]) is only partly legible; the final letters are uncertain. Hyphens at line ends ("Bo-", "demonstra-", "ali-", "om-") are kept as printed. "Reipub.melius" is printed without a space. The "impiorum" word has a small mark over the stem that may be a tilde; read as "impiorum". Dot-like marks after "habituri" and at the top of "ser" look like stains and are not transcribed. The text ends with a half-word "ser" as printed, and the catchword "monem" sits at the lower right.
